# Health outcomes and household income (fixture, cross-domain)

> **FIXTURE — not a real source.** Written for the test suite. The numbers illustrate a structure; they are not evidence about the world.

Household income is associated with a range of health outcomes. In longitudinal data,
lower income at baseline predicts higher incidence of several chronic conditions after
adjustment for age and sex. The gradient is continuous rather than a threshold: each
step down the income distribution is associated with somewhat worse outcomes. The
association is partly mediated by housing quality and access to care.
